deep.reconstruction:
This is not a mathematical page. It continues the observing log headed on the previous page 'Fundamentalsterne am M. T. 1819' (fundamental stars at the meridian instrument, presumably the Göttingen transit instrument, 'Mittagsfernrohr'). Each entry is a date (September 1819), a star, sometimes a small integer, and a number in seconds of time.

(1) The numbers are clock corrections (Uhrstand). For a transit observed at clock time T of a star of apparent right ascension alpha, the clock correction is Delta = alpha - T, in seconds; only the seconds part is written. Within one night the stars agree to about 0.1-0.4 s.

(2) The small integers (1, 2, 4, 4:, 6) are probably weights or numbers of wires observed. That reading is my inference.

(3) The entries run in right-ascension order through each night: Arcturus, alpha CrB, alpha Ser, alpha Sco, Capella, alpha Her, gamma/alpha/beta Aql, alpha And, gamma Peg, and then alpha Hydrae and Regulus the following morning.
- Capella (RA about 5h03m in 1819, dec +46 deg) appears between alpha Sco (about 16h18m) and alpha Her (about 17h06m). It must therefore have been observed at lower culmination, at RA+12h, about 17h03m. It is circumpolar at Gottingen (latitude 51.5 deg). This is my inference from the ordering.
- The seconds rise steadily with time, which reflects the clock rate.

(4) Daily progression of Delta, using alpha Aql (my computation):
- Sept 10: 31.27
- Sept 11: 33.19
- Sept 12: 35.96
- Sept 13: 38.78
- Sept 14: 41.98
- Sept 15: 45.13
- Rate: (45.13-31.27)/5, about 2.77 s/day, slowly increasing from about 1.9 to about 3.2 s/day.
- Sept 9 (about 5.3) to Sept 10 (31.3) shows a jump of about 26 s. Likewise Sept 15 (about 45) to Sept 16 (2.65), and the values on Sept 18-24, show that the clock was reset or that a different zero or clock was used. The same kind of reset occurs on the previous page (Sept 5, 11.49 to 0.93).

(5) Sept 24 values:
- They are referred to alpha Oph = 0: Capella (lower culmination) +0.07, alpha Her -0.20, Aquila stars +1.3 to +1.4, alpha Cap +1.6/+1.7, alpha And/gamma Peg +4.4. Then alpha CrB +13.95 on the 25th.
- This implies a rate of about 4.37 s in 6.5 h of sidereal time, i.e. about 16 s/day (alpha CrB: 13.95 over about 22 h, about 15 s/day). The clock was evidently running very differently, or a different clock was in use.

(6) The right-hand fragmentary column ('(1823?) Dec. 17. 270 39' 5..., Sudliches..., Nordliche..., Die T..., eine Ver..., nebst Dreh..., Geben d..., und s...') is not on this folio. It is the edge of the facing page, the next folio, with its quaternion/rotation note.

Purpose: determining the clock correction and rate from fundamental-star transits, as routine observatory practice at Göttingen.
errors: No mathematical errors are assessable; this is raw data.

The internal scatter is mostly 0.1-0.3 s, but some entries are discordant: e.g. Sept 13 gamma Aql 39.03 against alpha Aql 38.78, and Sept 24 gamma Aql +1.27 against an expected ~+1.45 from the rate. This is ordinary observational scatter or star-place error.
There are apparent discontinuities (Sept 9 to 10, 15 to 16, and 21 to 24). These are clock resets or zero changes, not slips.

results.what: Clock correction and clock rate determined from meridian transits of fundamental stars, including Capella at lower culmination
results.modern_name: Determination of clock error (Uhrstand) and rate (Gang) by the transit method
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-19th century observatory practice (Bradley, Maskelyne, Bessel)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observing log of clock corrections from star transits at the Göttingen observatory in 1819, with no mathematics on the page. Gauss's observational activity at the meridian instruments in this period is well documented.

checkable.asserts: Mean clock rate from alpha Aql, Sept 10 to Sept 15, is about 2.77 s/day
Day-to-day increments of the alpha Aql clock correction are 1.92, 2.77, 2.82, 3.20, 3.15 s, so the rate is gradually increasing
Sept 24 rate from alpha Oph (0) to alpha And (+4.37) over about 6.5 h of sidereal time is about 16 s/day
Capella (RA about 5h03m in 1819) at lower culmination transits at about 17h03m sidereal time, consistent with its listed position between alpha Sco and alpha Her
Capella (dec about +45.9 deg) is circumpolar at Göttingen (latitude about 51.53 deg), so a lower-culmination transit is observable

transcription_corrections: The whole right-hand column fragment '(1823?) Dec. 17. 270 39' 5 / 21 4 / 28 5 / Südliches / Nördliche / Die T.. / eine Ver.. / nebst Dreh.. / Geben d.. / und s..' belongs to the facing (next) folio visible at the image edge, not to this page.
Sept 24 'alpha Capric +1.70' is written as alpha-prime (alpha^1) Capric, paired with the following alpha^2 Capric +1.60.
Sept 9 'gamma Aquil -5.40': the dash is likely a stray mark or a ditto-type mark, not a negative sign, since the value fits the sequence at +5.40.
